label: Monado MIC
title: Monado MIC (Valve Index)
intro: The MIC calibration recordings of the Monado SLAM Datasets, made with a Valve Index headset: its front fisheye pair and its IMU, 8 camera-only and 8 camera + IMU recordings.
reading: Runs. We ran MVIS 0.4.1 (development version of 2026-11-26) on all 16 recordings, and Kalibr and Basalt on the 8 camera-only recordings, on 2026-11-27. The camera + IMU solves of Kalibr and Basalt are from October 2026. That Kalibr run uses its scale-misalignment IMU model, with a change that starts its spline from both cameras.

Accelerometer scale. On the camera + IMU recordings MVIS and Kalibr give an accelerometer scale of 1.055 to 1.066 on the three axes, and Basalt 1.017 to 1.024. We haven't established why the tools differ.

Chart centre. Each chart is centred on the Monado authors' own Basalt calibration of this headset, made from one recording: extras/calibration.raw.json for the camera–IMU distance, baseline and time offset, and its kb4 version (calibration.json) for the intrinsics. Their IMU terms are not used: the released recordings appear to carry the authors' IMU correction already, so those charts, and t_ga, are centred on the MVIS median.
no_repeatability: This study has no repeatability cells: they are computed for the leaderboard batch only. Each tool's spread over the 8 recordings of a family is in Parameters by sensor.
study_note: Separate study (batch 2026-11-27): MVIS, Kalibr and Basalt on the 8 MIC camera-only and 8 camera + IMU recordings, run outside the leaderboard batch, so it has no row here.

families.title: cam0 + cam1 stereo
families.read_first: Each tool calibrates both cameras and their baseline from the images alone, on the 8 camcalib recordings.
notes: Every tool ran on the same 8 recordings, each with its own camera model: MVIS equidistant, Kalibr pinhole-equi and Basalt kb4, the same polynomial.

families.title: cam0 + cam1 + IMU
families.read_first: MVIS starts from its camera-only result of the same round and refines the intrinsics. Kalibr's intrinsics and baselines are inputs from its own camera calibration on the same camera + IMU recording; its td, lever and IMU intrinsics are solved given them.
